\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{آواز} \fa{خواندن} (âvâz khândan)}{آواز خواندن (âvâz khândan)}]{\fa{آواز} \fa{خواندن} (âvâz khândan) — to sing}

\label{lesson:FA-C519-avaz-khandan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to play, then the Persian for to tune.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{آواز} \fa{خواندن}}
\textbf{\fa{آواز} \fa{خواندن}} (\emph{âvâz khândan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to sing\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مادرم} \fa{در} \fa{آشپزخانه} \fa{آواز} \fa{میخواند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mâdaram dar âshpazkhâne âvâz mikhânad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My mother sings in the kitchen.
\end{quote}

\emph{âvâz} 'song, voice' + \emph{khândan} 'to read, to sing'; present stem \emph{khân-}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{âvâz} is inherited: EtymDB traces it to a Middle Persian word for 'voice, sound, tune' and lists Latin \emph{vōx}, 'voice', as a cousin (EtymDB). \emph{khândan} is inherited too.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{âvâz khândan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{âvâz khândan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{âvâz khândan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to play, then the Persian for to tune, then say \emph{âvâz khândan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{آواز} \fa{خواندن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To sing\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{زمزمه} \fa{کردن} (zemzeme kardan)}{زمزمه کردن (zemzeme kardan)}]{\fa{زمزمه} \fa{کردن} (zemzeme kardan) — to hum, to murmur}

\label{lesson:FA-C519-zemzeme-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to tune, then the Persian for to sing.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{زمزمه} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{زمزمه} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{zemzeme kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to hum, to murmur\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{در} \fa{حمام} \fa{آهنگ} \fa{زمزمه} \fa{میکند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u dar hammâm âhang zemzeme mikonad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He hums tunes in the bath.
\end{quote}

\emph{zemzeme} 'a murmur' + \emph{kardan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{zemzeme} is a loan, usually traced to Arabic \emph{zamzama}, 'a low murmuring'. EtymDB has no entry for it. \emph{kardan} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zemzeme kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zemzeme kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{zemzeme kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to tune, then the Persian for to sing, then say \emph{zemzeme kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{زمزمه} \fa{کردن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To hum, to murmur\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ترانه} (tarâne)}{ترانه (tarâne)}]{\fa{ترانه} (tarâne) — a song (popular)}

\label{lesson:FA-C519-tarane}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to sing, then the Persian for to hum.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ترانه}}
\textbf{\fa{ترانه}} (\emph{tarâne}) — \textquotedblleft{}a song (popular)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{این} \fa{ترانه} \fa{را} \fa{از} \fa{رادیو} \fa{شنیدم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{in tarâne râ az râdiyo shenidam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I heard this song on the radio.
\end{quote}

A popular song; \emph{âhang} is the tune, \emph{tarâne} the song with words.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tarâne} is usually taken as a native Persian word for a song, but EtymDB lists it without a source, and its origin is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tarâne}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tarâne}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{tarâne}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to sing, then the Persian for to hum, then say \emph{tarâne} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{ترانه} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A song (popular)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ریتم} (ritm)}{ریتم (ritm)}]{\fa{ریتم} (ritm) — rhythm}

\label{lesson:FA-C519-ritm}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to hum, then the Persian for a song.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ریتم}}
\textbf{\fa{ریتم}} (\emph{ritm}) — \textquotedblleft{}rhythm\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بچه} \fa{ها} \fa{با} \fa{ریتم} \fa{موسیقی} \fa{دست} \fa{میزدند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bachchehâ bâ ritm-e musiqi dast mizadand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The children were clapping along to the music.
\end{quote}

Plural \emph{ritmhâ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ritm} is a modern loan, usually traced to French \emph{rythme}, 'rhythm'. EtymDB has no entry for the Persian word.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ritm}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ritm}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{ritm}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to hum, then the Persian for a song, then say \emph{ritm} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{ریتم} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Rhythm\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{نت} (not)}{نت (not)}]{\fa{نت} (not) — a musical note; sheet music}

\label{lesson:FA-C519-not}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a song, then the Persian for rhythm.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{نت}}
\textbf{\fa{نت}} (\emph{not}) — \textquotedblleft{}a musical note; sheet music\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{بدون} \fa{نت} \fa{پیانو} \fa{میزند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u bedun-e not piyâno mizanad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He plays the piano without sheet music.
\end{quote}

\emph{not khândan} — to read music.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{not} is a loan, usually traced to French \emph{note}, 'note'. EtymDB links the spelling only to English \emph{net}, a different word.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{not}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{not}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{not}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a song, then the Persian for rhythm, then say \emph{not} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
